title: Bounded Binary Arithmetic Transport
statement: Let $Q,T$ be types with decidable equality, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $increase$ be a Boolean, let $i$ be one of three digit-bank indices, and let $w,v$ be Boolean words. Suppose that applying fixed-width increment to $w$ when $increase$ is true, and fixed-width decrement otherwise, returns $v$, and that $v$ and $w$ have the same length. If a four-tape configuration $d$ is in the running state and its selected digit bank stores the encoded word $w$ relative to that tape's head position, then the corresponding embedded arithmetic machine reaches, within $2|w|+2$ steps, the configuration in the done-true state with that bank storing the encoding of $v$ and all other tape contents unchanged. Before that time it never has either done state, and throughout the run each tape head moves by at most $|w|+1$ from its initial position.
hypotheses_covered: An index $i$ among three digit-bank indices
The selected fixed-width increment or decrement of $w$ equals $v$
A four-tape configuration $d$ in the running state
The selected digit bank of $d$ stores the encoding of $w$ relative to its head position
